parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The graphs $y=\operatorname{cosec}x$ and $y=1+e^{-x/2}$ have exactly two intersections for $0<x<\pi$.
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Sketch a relevant graph, e.g. $y=\operatorname{cosec}x$ — B1. Guidance: $\operatorname{cosec}x$ U-shaped, roughly symmetrical about $x=\pi/2$, $y(\pi/2)=1$, and domain at least $(\pi/6,5\pi/6)$.

Sketch a second relevant graph, e.g. $y=1+e^{-x/2}$, and justify the given statement — B1. Guidance: exponential graph needs $y(0)=2$, negative gradient, always increasing, and $y(\pi)>1$; mark intersections with dots/crosses or say roots are at points of intersection, or equivalent. The internally inconsistent words “negative gradient, always increasing” are retained as printed.
